parameterNotes.service: the service whose large responses hung; the hang share is per service, and this is the one the overlay was rebuilt under.
parameterNotes.pod: the pod on the rebuilt path; the interface that still advertises the larger MTU belongs to it, which no series can say.
parameterNotes.interfaceMtu: what the pod's interface still advertises, which is why the segments left at that size; the reading is the hang share, not the ceiling.
parameterNotes.remediatedMtu: the path MTU the repair sets, stated for a replay; the two readings are the hang and the health check, and neither moves with this number.

groundTruth.rootCauseReason: The overlay was rebuilt onto a path whose MTU is 1,400 bytes while the pod's interface still advertises 1,500. A large response leaves in full-size segments, the router on the new path -- which this case's graph carries as `routes` -- drops the fragments it cannot forward, and the connection sits waiting for bytes that will never arrive -- so the request hangs rather than failing. Responses that fit in one segment are unaffected, which is why the health check stayed green while real traffic stalled.

rootCauseIndicators.description: every request whose response exceeds one segment hangs, which is a size threshold rather than a rate
the health check stays green throughout, because its response is small enough to fit

causalChain.mechanism: the pod sends full-size segments onto a path that drops them, so every response larger than one segment arrives as a first segment and nothing else, and the request hangs until it times out

evidenceCheckpoints.description: every large request hangs -- a share of one, because the threshold is a size and not a rate
small payloads are unaffected, which is the control that turns a stall into a size threshold rather than a broken network
the health check never failed, because its own response fits in one segment -- which is why an orchestrator saw nothing wrong
the path's MTU after the overlay was rebuilt, cited from the case's own parameters; the pod's interface is 100 bytes larger, which is the whole fault

remediation.action: lower the pod interface's MTU to 1,380 so its segments fit inside the path's 1,400-byte MTU with room for the tunnel header
probe with a payload larger than one segment rather than only with a health check, so a black hole cannot pass as healthy

sli.none: the blackhole shows up as the share of large requests that hang, the share of small ones that fail and the share of health checks that pass -- three shares and no duration among them.

query: Catalog service requests larger than about 1,400 bytes hang while its health checks stay green. What is the root cause, and why did the health check not see it?
